- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially after spikes.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model often underestimates; adjust upward, particularly if price has recently dipped.
- Model frequently overreacts to short-term sentiment shifts — especially after a spike — leading to overshoot; apply a lagged smoothing or dampen momentum in forecast.
- Mean reversion is evident in 30d forecasts: model often fails to capture gradual pullback after highs; add a mild downward bias toward mid-range of recent history.
- Forecasts tend to be too optimistic in early horizon (e.g., 1–3 days ahead) when sentiment is volatile; reduce forecast magnitude for short-term horizons if sentiment is mixed or trending down.
- If sentiment history shows repeated oscillation (e.g., alternating +0.33/-0.33), model may overfit noise; use sentiment-weighted moving average to filter out erratic swings.
